name: WordPress VoiceOvers v2.0 - Multilingual Google Cloud TTS

nodes.name: Workflow Configuration
nodes.notes: Single place for every setting: Sheet, Cloud Run, bucket, languages, voices, page IDs, batch size, retries.

nodes.name: Plan Queue Changes
nodes.notes: Compares each post fingerprint with the queue. New or changed content becomes a pending row with Attempts reset to 0. Does nothing while another run holds the lock.

nodes.name: Select Pending & Retryable Jobs
nodes.notes: Pending first (oldest article first), then failed jobs under the attempt limit and past the cooldown. Limited to maxJobsPerRun.

nodes.name: Acquire Run Lock
nodes.notes: Soft lock stored in the queue sheet. Reduces overlapping runs but is not atomic - see README, Known limitations.

nodes.name: No Jobs to Process
nodes.notes: Empty queue, nothing to retry yet, or another run holds the lock. The input item says which.

nodes.name: Loop Over Jobs
nodes.notes: Batch size MUST stay 1: every iteration has to hand exactly one item back to this node.

nodes.name: Prepare Job
nodes.notes: Validates the job. Later nodes reference it with $('Prepare Job').item (item linking), never .first().

nodes.name: Fetch Current Article
nodes.notes: Re-fetches the article by ID so the audio always matches the current text.

nodes.name: Check Existing Audio
nodes.notes: HEAD request for the versioned filename. A 404 is a normal answer (no audio yet).

nodes.name: Translate Text Chunk
nodes.notes: Regular-output error handling on purpose: one failed chunk must not create a second path. Join Translated Chunks validates every chunk.

nodes.name: Join Translated Chunks
nodes.notes: Never throws and always returns exactly one item. A translation problem is passed on as translationError and raised by Prepare TTS Request.

nodes.name: Generate VoiceOver (Cloud Run)
nodes.notes: Same endpoint and fields as v1.3: text, language, voice, filename. Header Auth credential as in v1.3 (set Authentication to None if your service is public).

nodes.name: Verify Generated Audio
nodes.notes: Fails (and retries) unless the new file answers with HTTP 2xx.

nodes.name: Build Updated Page Content
nodes.notes: Replaces only this article's marked block (v2 and v1.x markers). Everything else on the page is preserved.

nodes.name: Reconcile Article Status
nodes.notes: Article-level status: done (all languages), partial (some), failed, pending, processing.

nodes.name: Mark Job as Done
nodes.notes: Only reached after audio generation, verification and publication all succeeded.

nodes.name: Collect Job Failures
nodes.notes: Error bus: the error output of every node in the job loop ends here.

nodes.name: Build Failure Update
nodes.notes: Never throws and always returns exactly ONE item, whatever arrives on the error bus. Identifies the job through $('Prepare Job') and formats the error for the queue.

parameters.content:
# WordPress VoiceOvers v2.0 – Batch & Resilient Multilingual

Turns WordPress articles into audio in every configured language with Google Cloud Translation, Text-to-Speech (Cloud Run) and Cloud Storage, then publishes HTML5 players on dedicated WordPress pages. Processes up to 12 article-language jobs per run, retries failures safely and regenerates audio only when an article changes.

## How It Works

1. **Fetch** – Reads recent WordPress posts on a daily schedule (or manually).
2. **Detect Changes** – Builds a content fingerprint per post and upserts one queue row per article and language in Google Sheets.
3. **Select Jobs** – Picks pending jobs, plus failed jobs that are past the retry cooldown and under the attempt limit. A run lock prevents overlapping runs.
4. **Translate & Speak** – One loop handles every job: translate only when needed, then call Cloud Run `/long-tts`. Audio that already exists is reused.
5. **Verify & Publish** – Checks the audio URL, then replaces that article's player block on the language page.
6. **Track Status** – Marks `done` only after publication is confirmed. Failures keep the error, attempt count and retry time.

## Requirements

- WordPress with REST API and an application-password user that can edit pages (`unfiltered_html` for `<audio>`)
- Google Cloud: Translation, Text-to-Speech, Cloud Run, Cloud Storage
- Public audio URL (bucket or CDN)
- Google Sheet with the queue header row
- Cloud Run `POST /long-tts` accepting `text`, `language`, `voice`, `filename`

## Setup

1. Create the Sheet tab and header row from the README.
2. Edit **Workflow Configuration**: sheet ID, Cloud Run URL, bucket, page IDs, languages.
3. Connect credentials: WordPress, Google service account (Sheets + Translate), Header Auth for Cloud Run (if your service requires a key).
4. Run manually with a small batch, check the Sheet, then activate the schedule.
5. Keep **Loop Over Jobs** at batch size 1 and run only one execution at a time.

## Customization

Add languages, voices, labels and filename patterns in **Workflow Configuration**. Change the schedule in **Daily Schedule**.

## Documentation & Support

[Documentation & Setup Guide](https://app.notion.com/p/paoloronco/WordPress-VoiceOvers-415f0ba27c32816a960ac1a8a51dc5f9)

For custom implementation, workflow integration, troubleshooting or consulting services, contact me through [paoloronco.it](https://paoloronco.it).

---

**Note:** This template requires your own Google Cloud infrastructure and credentials. Cloud services may incur usage costs. Review all configuration values and permissions before activating the workflow.

## 1. Fetch WordPress Articles
Start manually or on schedule, load the shared configuration and fetch recent posts.

## 2. Detect Changes & Build Processing Queue
Fingerprint each post and create or reset one queue row per article and language. Unchanged articles are skipped.

## 3. Select Pending & Retryable Jobs
Read the queue, take up to 12 jobs (pending first, then retries after cooldown) and acquire the run lock.

## 4. Multilingual Translation & TTS
One loop and one pipeline for every language: re-fetch the article, reuse existing audio, translate only when needed and call Cloud Run.

## 5. Verify Audio & Publish to WordPress
Confirm the audio file is reachable, then replace or append this article's player and confirm it was saved.

## 6. Update Status & Error Handling
Mark jobs done, record failures with attempts and error text, then release the lock and refresh article-level status. Error paths run along the bottom.
